subject: [Escalation] Solstice Payments — AZ1 high latency & error spike (exec bridge requested)
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@solsticepay.com>
To: support@redwood.inference, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout — AZ1

Hi Olga / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a rising 5xx rate for API keys provisioned in us-east-1 (AZ1) starting ~08:45 PDT. Checkout times are spiking to 6–8s and a subset of transactions are failing with 502/504 intermittently. We're currently routing ~18% of traffic through Redwood for payment scoring — this is starting to impact customer payments.

Attached are a short error log and traces from our service for the 09:00–09:10 window. Our infra team has checked health at our side; no obvious network changes. Can you confirm status on your side and whether there's an active remediation plan? We need an ETA.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Infrastructure, Solstice Payments

attachments:
- solstice_az1_error_log_0618.txt (text)
- traces_spike_0618.json (json)
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout — AZ1

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're seeing matching latency and an error-rate bump on our AZ1 pool starting ~08:40 PDT. I have pulled the initial telemetry and kicked off a high-priority incident.

Immediate next steps:
- Rishi (SRE) is on a deep-dive to identify root cause (kernel metrics, queue saturation, KV cache pressure).
- We will open a 15-min exec bridge and include their SRE + our on-call.
- I'll share a short incident summary and an ETA for mitigation within 20 mins.

Can you confirm whether Solstice can divert traffic to us-east-2 temporarily if we request a geo-steer? If yes, we might ask for a short redirect while we clear AZ1.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout — AZ1

On Mon, Jun 18, 2028 at 09:18 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're seeing matching latency...

Quick summary from the first 10m of telemetry:
- AZ1 (host pool az1-eu/az1-us-east) shows memory-backed KV cache thrashing for hot prefixes; sustained CPU queuing on two GPU nodes (g4x-24).
- Autoscaler attempted a scale-up but was blocked by internal quota exhaustion for the reserved pool in AZ1 (ticket opened).
- Error signatures look like tokenization OOMs upstream + a small set of 5xx (gateway timeouts) when requests miss cache and escalate compute.

Proposed immediate mitigation (can do in parallel):
1) Open exec bridge (we need Marissa for customer comms and Hannah for routing policy decision).
2) Temporarily route Solstice traffic to us-east-2 model variants (we have capacity there).
3) Clear cache slices for the affected prefixes and roll a light-weight restart on the two contended nodes.

I can have a mitigation plan in the bridge and an ETA (~25–30 min) once we confirm steer permissions.

—Rishi

- PagerDuty incident: PD-8421 (updates posted there)

We'll also prepare provisional goodwill credit language if the issue persists beyond the bridge window.

—Marissa

Joining now. We can accept a geo-steer to us-east-2 for up to 45 minutes. Carlos will join the bridge as our on-call. We need to confirm the user impact window and whether payment consistency (idempotency keys) will be preserved.

Samantha
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@solsticepay.com>, carlos.ops@solsticepay.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout — AZ1

Update from bridge:
- We executed a controlled geo-steer of Solstice traffic to us-east-2 at 09:42 PDT. Initial telemetry shows tail latency back to normal within 5–6 minutes for 70% of requests.
- We drained two contended nodes and rehydrated KV caches. CPU queuing subsided after the drain.
- A quota exhaustion bug prevented autoscaler from adding temporary nodes in AZ1; engineering has an immediate hotfix and the cloud quota has been requested as a follow-up item.

Next steps:
1) Rishi's team will run a post-mortem and share a mitigation-runbook for prefix-level cache pressure by EOD.
2) Marissa will prepare a customer-facing summary + goodwill credit proposal — we'll propose a one-month service credit tied to the affected token volume.
3) I'll escalate the quota issue to Product Ops to ensure reserved pools have buffer capacity for top-tier customers.

Samantha, thanks for flexibility on the steer — can you confirm acceptance of the proposed credit language once Marissa shares it?

—Olga
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@solsticepay.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 01:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike impacting checkout — AZ1 (post-incident summary)

Samantha — follow-up after today's bridge. Apologies again for the disruption. Brief summary and actions (concise):
- Incident window: 08:40–09:42 PDT (US-East AZ1). Root cause: KV cache thrash + blocked autoscale due to reserved-pool quota bug.
- Impact: transient latency spikes and ~2.7% error-rate delta on Solstice's production keys; peak customer-facing failures estimated at ~0.9% of transactions.
- Mitigation executed: geo-steer → us-east-2 (09:42), cache rehydration and node drain, hotfix deployed to prevent autoscale blockage.

Action items / commitments:
- Engineering will deliver a runbook for cache pressure and an automation to preemptively allocate temporary capacity for top-tier accounts by 2028-06-25.
- Product Ops to revise reserved-pool buffer policy and report back by 2028-06-22.
- Customer credit: proposing 1 month of usage credit proportional to the affected token volume (draft in Drive link above). Awaiting confirmation.

Again — we'll post the post-mortem and timeline in the Drive folder and update the HubSpot ticket with the credit proposal. If you prefer a synchronous exec review with your leadership, we can schedule one.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
